rationale.general_comments:
2025

Marsh. Renewal. Caroline Brock.
Alpha renewal. Restructure on the underlying. Further broadening of the primary policy which helps us. No claims. Target pricing given which we followed. Led by The Hartford.

2024
First renewal of A side Marsh opportunity on NAB
We came off the D&O several years ago due to the RC exclusion not being tight enough
NAB decided to go with side A placement in 2022-23  year and Marsh approached us with an Alpha opportunity.
No claims/circs of any concern

rationale.reason_comments:
2025 Update
Supportive of the Alpha facility. No claims issues. Financially strong. Good sustainability credentials. Improving risk farmwork. String physical controls.

Ed comments:
Longstanding London Placement, though reconfigured their Risk Transfer approach in 2022-23 due to Pricing and availability of stable capacity from Australian & London Market -  impressive organisation. Financially very stable with excellent Capital Ratios, strong Liquidity Ratios and low NPL's Has Grown Gross revenues on back of Strong Margins due to Interest Income Growth from Interest Rate Increases on Gross basis - Non Interest income is up very Modestly.

Governance is strong as is the share price Market Cap growth due to earning power the NIM gives then during 2023 Year . Target list account. Minimal wording amendments this year. Robust risk and compliance framework. Line size in line with strategy. Pricing good for attachment point and coverage. Primary retentions increased. No sanctions issues. Claims record on file. - little of concern to A side at the time of writing..
  
Do have an AUSTRAC EU (Enforceable undertaking) iro AML/KYC which began in April 2022.

risk_info.comments:
Acrophyte Asset Management Pte. Ltd., incoporated in Singapore on 22 June 2022 (UEN 202221501M). Private company limited by shares.

**Wholly Owned By**: Tang Organization Pte. Ltd., which is in turn controlled by Mr. Gordon Tang and Mrs. Celine Tang

**Acrophyte Asset Management,** an entity controlled by property tycoon Gordon Tang, has agreed to acquire the manager of Suntec Real Estate Investment Trust (Suntec REIT) from ESR Group for S$190 million (approximately $147 million USD).
The transaction involves Acrophyte Asset Management, controlled by Gordon Tang, purchasing ESR Trust Management (Suntec) Limited from ESR Group subsidiaries for S$190 million, a price linked to the net asset value. The acquisition is conditional on receiving approval from the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS). This move increases Gordon Tang's involvement in Suntec REIT, where he already holds a substantial stake. Acrophyte plans to evaluate strategies and introduce initiatives to enhance value after the deal is completed. This acquisition follows a similar action earlier in the year where Acrophyte acquired the manager of ARA US Hospitality Trust from ESR.

**About Suntec REIT**:
Listed on 9 December 2004, Suntec REIT holds properties in Suntec City, Singapore’s largest integrated commercial development (including one of Singapore’s largest shopping mall), a 66.3% interest in Suntec Singapore Convention & Exhibition Centre, a one-third interest in One Raffles Quay and a one-third interest in Marina Bay Financial Centre Towers 1 and 2 and the Marina Bay Link Mall. Suntec REIT holds a 100% interest in a commercial building located at 177 Pacific Highway, Sydney, a 100% interest in a commercial building located at 21 Harris Street, Pyrmont, Sydney, a 50.0% interest in Southgate Complex, Melbourne, a 50.0% interest in a commercial building located at Olderfleet 477 Collins Street, Melbourne and a 100% interest in a commercial building located at 55 Currie Street, Adelaide, Australia. Suntec REIT also holds a 50.0% interest in Nova Properties and a 100% interest in The Minster Building both located in London, United Kingdom.
